name: GeNTE
description: Gender inequality is embedded in our communication practices and perpetuated in translation technologies. This becomes particularly apparent when translating into grammatical gender languages, where machine translation (MT) often defaults to masculine and stereotypical representations by making undue binary gender assumptions. Our work addresses the rising demand for inclusive language by focusing head-on on gender-neutral translation from English to Italian. We start from the essentials: proposing a dedicated benchmark and exploring automated evaluation methods. First, we introduce GeNTE, a natural, bilingual test set for gender-neutral translation, whose creation was informed by a survey on the perception and use of neutral language. Based on GeNTE, we then overview existing reference-based evaluation approaches, highlight their limits, and propose a reference-free method more suitable to assess gender-neutral translation.
evaluation_method: reference-free (primary proposed), supplemented by BLEU and human evaluation for reference-based comparisons
general_score_metric: reference-free gender-neutrality score (proposed) / BLEU for reference-based comparisons
reputation: A specialized, recently proposed benchmark valued in research on gender-neutral translation, particularly for English→Italian studies, but with limited mainstream adoption so far.
notes: Small, language-pair–specific test set (English→Italian); assessing gender-neutral translation often requires human judgments and cultural context, limiting purely automatic evaluation.
